ja: 人の目は約100万色以上を見分けられるとされる。
easy: Human eyes can tell apart about a million colors or more.
std: The human eye is thought to distinguish around a million or more colors.

ja: 舌の場所によって感じる味が決まっているという「味覚地図」は誤り。どの場所でもすべての味を感じる。
easy: The 'tongue map' is wrong. All parts of the tongue can taste every taste.
std: The 'tongue map' is a myth: all taste qualities can be sensed across all areas of the tongue.

ja: 生まれたばかりの赤ちゃんのひざのお皿（膝蓋骨）は軟骨で、骨になるのは数年後。
easy: Babies' kneecaps are soft at first. They turn into bone after a few years.
std: A newborn's kneecaps are made of cartilage and only ossify into bone over the following years.

ja: 人の足には片足だけで26個の骨がある。両足で全身の骨の約4分の1になる。
easy: Each foot has 26 bones. Your feet have about a quarter of all your bones.
std: Each human foot contains 26 bones, so the feet together hold about a quarter of the body's bones.

ja: ABO式の血液型は、1901年にオーストリアのラントシュタイナーが発見した。
easy: The ABO blood groups were discovered in 1901.
std: Karl Landsteiner discovered the ABO blood group system in 1901.

ja: 肝臓は一部を切り取っても再生できる珍しい臓器。
easy: The liver can grow back after part of it is removed.
std: The liver can regenerate after a large part of it has been removed.

ja: 世界初のワクチンは、1796年にジェンナーが牛痘を使って天然痘を防いだもの。vaccine の vacca はラテン語で「牛」。
easy: The first vaccine was made in 1796 using cowpox. 'Vacca' means cow in Latin.
std: Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine in 1796 using cowpox to protect against smallpox; 'vaccine' comes from Latin vacca, 'cow'.

ja: しゃっくりは、横隔膜が急に縮むことで起こる。その直後に声帯が閉じて「ヒック」という音が出る。
easy: Hiccups happen when a muscle under your lungs suddenly tightens.
std: A hiccup is a sudden contraction of the diaphragm followed by the vocal cords snapping shut, which makes the 'hic' sound.

ja: ペニシリンは1928年、フレミングが休暇から戻って、カビが生えた実験皿で細菌が育っていないのに気づいて発見された。
easy: Penicillin was found in 1928 when Fleming saw that mold stopped bacteria in a dish.
std: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 after noticing that mold had killed bacteria in a culture dish.

ja: X線は1895年にレントゲンが発見した。最初のX線写真の一つは妻の手で、指輪が写っていた。
easy: X-rays were found in 1895. One of the first X-ray pictures showed Röntgen's wife's hand and ring.
std: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895; one of the first X-ray images showed his wife's hand, wedding ring included.

ja: くしゃみの速さは時速数十kmほど。かつて言われた「時速160km」は大げさとされる。
easy: A sneeze is fast, but not as fast as 160 km per hour, as some people say.
std: Sneezes expel air at tens of kilometers per hour; popular claims of 160 km/h are exaggerated.

ja: 人は朝起きたときのほうが、夜より身長が約1cm高い。背骨の間の軟骨が昼間に縮むため。
easy: You are about 1 cm taller in the morning than at night.
std: People are about a centimeter taller in the morning, as the discs in the spine compress during the day.

ja: 鳥肌は、毛を逆立てて体を大きく見せたり温めたりした祖先のなごりと考えられている。
easy: Goosebumps may come from our hairy ancestors. Raising hair helped them stay warm.
std: Goosebumps are thought to be a leftover reflex from ancestors who fluffed up body hair for warmth or to look bigger.

ja: 人の腸の中には、数十兆個の細菌がすんでいる。
easy: Tens of trillions of bacteria live in your gut.
std: The human gut hosts tens of trillions of bacteria.

ja: 笑いは伝染しやすい。人は一人でいるときより、誰かと一緒のときに30倍ほどよく笑うという研究がある。
easy: People laugh about 30 times more with others than when they are alone.
std: Research suggests people are around 30 times more likely to laugh when with others than when alone.

ja: 「アイスクリーム頭痛」は、冷たいものが口の上あごを冷やし、血管が急に変化して起こると考えられている。
easy: 'Brain freeze' happens when something cold touches the top of your mouth.
std: 'Brain freeze' is thought to occur when cold food chills the roof of the mouth, causing a rapid change in blood vessels.

ja: 人は食べ物がなくても数週間生きられることがあるが、水がないと数日しかもたない。
easy: People can live weeks without food, but only a few days without water.
std: Humans can survive several weeks without food but only a few days without water.

ja: 人間は長距離走が得意な動物で、汗をかいて体を冷やせるため、暑い中では馬より長く走り続けられることがある。
easy: Humans are good long-distance runners. On hot days, people can sometimes outrun horses.
std: Thanks to sweating, humans are excellent endurance runners and can outlast horses over long distances in hot weather.

ja: 耳の奥の三半規管は、体のバランスを保つ働きをしている。乗り物酔いは、目と耳からの情報のずれで起こるとされる。
easy: Parts of your inner ear help with balance. Motion sickness comes from your eyes and ears disagreeing.
std: The inner ear's semicircular canals help maintain balance; motion sickness is thought to arise from a mismatch between visual and inner-ear signals.

ja: 人の体で最も小さい骨は、耳の中にある「あぶみ骨」。
easy: The smallest bone in your body is in your ear.
std: The smallest bone in the human body is the stapes, in the middle ear.

ja: わさびの辛さは揮発する成分によるため、すりおろしてから時間がたつと弱くなる。
easy: Wasabi loses its heat soon after it is grated.
std: Wasabi's pungency comes from volatile compounds, so it fades within minutes of grating.

ja: バナナは植物学的にはベリー（液果）の仲間。一方、イチゴはベリーではない。
easy: In science, a banana is a berry, but a strawberry is not.
std: Botanically, bananas are berries, while strawberries are not.

ja: ジャガイモは南米アンデスが原産。ヨーロッパに広まったのは16世紀以降。
easy: Potatoes come from the Andes in South America. They came to Europe in the 1500s.
std: Potatoes were domesticated in the Andes of South America and reached Europe in the 16th century.

ja: すしのもとは、魚を米と一緒に発酵させて保存する東南アジアの方法とされる。今の握りずしは江戸時代の「早ずし」から。
easy: Sushi started as a way to keep fish in rice. Today's sushi comes from Edo-period fast food.
std: Sushi began as a method of preserving fish in fermented rice; modern nigiri sushi developed as fast food in Edo-period Tokyo.

ja: ナポリタンは日本で生まれたスパゲッティ料理。横浜のホテルニューグランドが発祥とされる。
easy: Spaghetti Napolitan was created in Japan, at a hotel in Yokohama.
std: Spaghetti Napolitan is a Japanese creation, said to have originated at the Hotel New Grand in Yokohama.

ja: あんパンは1874年、東京・銀座の木村屋（現・木村屋總本店）が考案した。
easy: Anpan, bread with sweet bean paste, was made in Ginza, Tokyo, in 1874.
std: Anpan, a bun filled with sweet red bean paste, was created in 1874 by Kimuraya bakery in Ginza, Tokyo.

ja: イタリアのパスタにトマトソースが使われるようになったのは、トマトが新大陸から伝わった後の18〜19世紀ごろ。
easy: Italians began putting tomato sauce on pasta only about 200 to 300 years ago.
std: Tomato sauce became common on Italian pasta only in the 18th and 19th centuries, after tomatoes arrived from the Americas.

ja: マルゲリータ・ピザの赤・白・緑は、イタリア国旗の色と同じ。
easy: Pizza Margherita is red, white, and green, like the Italian flag.
std: Pizza Margherita's tomato, mozzarella and basil echo the red, white and green of the Italian flag.

ja: チョコレートは、もともと中米で苦い飲み物として飲まれていた。固形の板チョコが作られたのは19世紀。
easy: Chocolate was first a bitter drink in Central America. Chocolate bars came in the 1800s.
std: Chocolate was first consumed as a bitter drink in Mesoamerica; solid chocolate bars were developed in the 19th century.

ja: 唐辛子の辛さは「スコヴィル値」で表す。辛さの成分カプサイシンは、鳥にはほとんど辛く感じないとされる。
easy: Chili heat is measured in Scoville units. Birds do not feel the heat.
std: Chili heat is measured in Scoville units; birds are largely insensitive to capsaicin, the compound that makes peppers hot.

ja: しょうゆは日本の代表的な調味料だが、そのもとは古代中国の「醤（ジャン）」とされる。
easy: Soy sauce is very Japanese, but it started from an old Chinese sauce.
std: Soy sauce is central to Japanese cooking but traces its origins to fermented sauces in ancient China.

ja: とんかつは、明治時代に西洋料理のカツレツをもとに日本で生まれた。
easy: Tonkatsu, a fried pork cutlet, was created in Japan from a Western dish.
std: Tonkatsu developed in Meiji-era Japan from the European cutlet.

ja: クロワッサンはフランスのパンとして有名だが、もとはオーストリアのキプフェルというパンがもとになったとされる。
easy: The croissant is French, but it probably came from an Austrian bread.
std: The croissant is associated with France but is thought to derive from the Austrian kipferl.

ja: ソフトクリームのコーンが広まったのは、1904年のセントルイス万博がきっかけという話が有名。
easy: Ice cream cones became popular at a world fair in 1904.
std: Ice cream cones are popularly said to have taken off at the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair.

ja: コンビニのおにぎりの「のりを別にした包装」は、パリッとしたのりのまま食べられるよう日本で工夫されたもの。
easy: Japanese convenience-store rice balls keep the seaweed separate so it stays crisp.
std: Japanese convenience-store onigiri use packaging that keeps the nori separate from the rice so it stays crisp.

ja: アボカドの名前は、メキシコのナワトル語の ahuacatl から来ている。
easy: 'Avocado' comes from a word in Nahuatl, a language of Mexico.
std: 'Avocado' comes from the Nahuatl word ahuacatl.

ja: 世界には7500種類以上のりんごの品種がある。日本の「ふじ」は世界で最も多く作られている品種の一つ。
easy: There are more than 7,500 kinds of apples. Japan's Fuji apple is grown all over the world.
std: There are over 7,500 apple cultivars; Japan's Fuji is one of the most widely grown in the world.

ja: ピーナッツは名前に「ナッツ」とつくが、豆の仲間。
easy: Peanuts are not nuts. They are beans.
std: Despite the name, peanuts are legumes, not true nuts.

ja: トマトは長い間、ヨーロッパの一部で毒があると考えられていた。
easy: In parts of Europe, people once thought tomatoes were poisonous.
std: Tomatoes were long regarded with suspicion in parts of Europe, where some believed them poisonous.

ja: 世界の人口の半分以上が、お米を主食にしている。
easy: More than half of the people in the world eat rice as their main food.
std: Rice is a staple food for more than half of the world's population.

ja: 「バーナム効果」：誰にでも当てはまる性格の説明を、自分だけにぴったりだと感じてしまう。
easy: We often think a general personality description fits us perfectly. This is the Barnum effect.
std: The Barnum effect is the tendency to accept vague, general personality descriptions as uniquely accurate about oneself.

ja: 「ハロー効果」：一つ目立つ長所があると、ほかの面まで良く見えてしまう。
easy: If someone has one great quality, we often think they are good in other ways too.
std: The halo effect is when one positive trait colors our overall impression of a person.

ja: 「傍観者効果」：周りに人が多いほど、困っている人を助ける人が出にくくなる。
easy: When many people are around, each person is less likely to help.
std: The bystander effect is the finding that people are less likely to help a victim when others are present.

ja: 「返報性」：人は何かをしてもらうと、お返しをしたくなる。試供品が効果的なのもこのため。
easy: When someone gives us something, we want to give something back.
std: The norm of reciprocity makes people feel obliged to return favors, which is one reason free samples work.

ja: 「単純接触効果」：何度も見たり聞いたりするだけで、そのものを好きになりやすい。
easy: We often start to like things just because we see them many times.
std: The mere-exposure effect means people tend to develop a preference for things simply because they are familiar.

ja: 「シロクマのことを考えないで」と言われると、かえって考えてしまう。思考を抑えようとすると逆効果になる現象。
easy: If someone tells you not to think of a white bear, you will think of it more.
std: Trying not to think of a white bear makes the thought come back more often, an example of ironic thought suppression.

ja: バスケットボールのパス回しを数えている人の多くは、画面を横切るゴリラの着ぐるみに気づかない。「見えないゴリラ」の実験。
easy: In one test, many people counting basketball passes did not see a person in a gorilla suit.
std: In the 'invisible gorilla' experiment, many viewers counting basketball passes failed to notice a person in a gorilla suit walking through the scene.

ja: 「マシュマロ実験」は子どもの我慢する力と将来の関係を調べた研究。のちの研究では、家庭環境の影響も大きいとされた。
easy: In the 'marshmallow test', children were asked to wait for a second treat. Later studies found family background also mattered.
std: The marshmallow test studied children's ability to delay gratification; later research found family background explained much of the link to later success.

ja: 「フレーミング効果」：「成功率90％」と「失敗率10％」は同じ意味なのに、受ける印象が変わる。
easy: '90% success' and '10% failure' mean the same, but they feel different.
std: The framing effect means identical information, such as '90 percent success' versus '10 percent failure', leads to different choices.

ja: 「計画錯誤」：人は作業にかかる時間を短く見積もりがち。過去に遅れた経験があっても繰り返す。
easy: People usually think tasks will take less time than they really do.
std: The planning fallacy is our tendency to underestimate how long tasks will take, even when past tasks ran late.

ja: 「フロー」：時間を忘れるほど何かに没頭している状態。難しさと自分の力がちょうど釣り合っているときに起こりやすい。
easy: 'Flow' is when you are so focused that you forget time. It happens when a task is not too easy and not too hard.
std: Flow is a state of deep absorption that tends to occur when a task's challenge matches one's skill level.

ja: 脳には約860億個の神経細胞（ニューロン）があると推定されている。
easy: The brain has about 86 billion nerve cells.
std: The human brain is estimated to contain about 86 billion neurons.

ja: 大人になっても、脳は学習によって変化し続ける。この性質を「神経可塑性」という。
easy: Even adult brains keep changing when we learn.
std: The brain keeps changing in response to learning throughout life, a property called neuroplasticity.

ja: ロンドンのタクシー運転手は、道を覚える訓練の後、記憶に関わる脳の部分（海馬の一部）が大きくなっていたという研究がある。
easy: London taxi drivers who learned all the streets had a larger part of the brain for memory.
std: Studies found that London taxi drivers, after memorizing the city's streets, had enlarged parts of the hippocampus.

ja: 頭の中で同じ曲が繰り返し流れる現象を英語で earworm（耳の虫）と呼ぶ。
easy: When a song keeps playing in your head, it is called an 'earworm'.
std: A tune that keeps replaying in your head is called an 'earworm'.

ja: あくびがうつるのは、共感の働きと関係があるという説がある。
easy: Yawns are catching. Some scientists think this is linked to empathy.
std: Contagious yawning may be linked to empathy, according to some researchers.

ja: 自然の中で過ごしたり、緑を眺めたりするだけでも、ストレスが下がるという研究が多くある。
easy: Spending time in nature, or even looking at trees, can lower stress.
std: Many studies suggest that time in nature, or even views of greenery, can reduce stress.

ja: 手で書いてノートをとると、パソコンで打つより内容の理解が深まるという研究がある。
easy: Some studies say writing notes by hand helps you understand more than typing.
std: Some studies suggest that taking notes by hand leads to better understanding than typing them.

ja: 独り言を言いながら探し物をすると、見つけやすくなるという実験がある。
easy: Saying the name of a thing out loud can help you find it faster.
std: Experiments suggest that saying the name of an object aloud can help people find it more quickly.

ja: 「ピーク・エンドの法則」：人は経験を、いちばん強く感じた瞬間と最後の印象でおもに判断する。
easy: We judge an experience mostly by its best or worst moment and by its end.
std: The peak–end rule says people judge an experience largely by its most intense moment and how it ended.
